description: Retrieve the top matching TV news clips for a query from the Internet Archive's Television News Archive: returns every fetched in-window clip, up to 3,000. Each clip includes show name, the station's display name — with its station ID when that name resolves to one — air timestamp, a 15-second transcript excerpt, and a direct link to view the full one-minute clip. Use after gdelt_search_tv to read the actual transcript content driving a coverage spike — pass a series' station value as stations here. GDELT answers TV windows in whole clock hours; clips it returns from outside an explicit startDatetime/endDatetime window are dropped. 3,000 is a hard per-call ceiling and GDELT offers no cursor: when a query fills it, re-query narrower startDatetime/endDatetime windows — the response hands back the exact windows to use. Archive coverage varies by station; use gdelt_list_tv_stations for station IDs and monitoring date ranges.

endDatetime.description: End datetime in GDELT format YYYYMMDDHHMMSS — exactly 14 digits, no separators (e.g. 20200131235959). Must pair with startDatetime; supplying only one of the two is rejected.

maxRecords.description: Maximum number of clips to fetch. Defaults to 50; values above 3000 run at 3000 with a limitClamp disclosure unless clamping is disabled. Every fetched in-window record is returned. 3000 is GDELT's hard per-call ceiling, with no cursor; split a query that fills it into narrower startDatetime/endDatetime windows.

query.description: Search query for TV transcript content. Same TV operators as gdelt_search_tv: station:CNN, network:CBS, market:"National", show:"Anderson Cooper", context:"vaccine".

sort.description: Sort order: relevance (default), dateDesc (newest first), dateAsc (oldest first).

startDatetime.description: Start datetime in GDELT format YYYYMMDDHHMMSS — exactly 14 digits, no separators (e.g. 20200101000000). Must pair with endDatetime; supplying only one of the two is rejected.

stations.description: Station IDs to filter to (e.g. ["CNN", "FOXNEWS"]). Alternatively use station:, network:, or quoted market: selectors in query. A selector is required; use gdelt_list_tv_stations for station IDs, networks, markets, and monitoring dates.

timespan.description: Time window, e.g. "1m", "6m". Ignored when startDatetime/endDatetime are set. TV coverage varies by station; check monitoring dates with gdelt_list_tv_stations.

name: gdelt_get_tv_clips

clips.description: Matching TV clips sorted per the sort parameter.

items.description: A single TV news clip with transcript excerpt and archive link.

archiveUrl.description: Internet Archive URL to view the full 1-minute clip.

station.description: Station ID — the value the stations input and the station: operator take (e.g. "FOXNEWS"). Absent when GDELT's label for the station could not be resolved to an ID; notice says why.

stationName.description: GDELT's display label for the station (e.g. "FOX News"). Empty when GDELT returned the clip without one; notice says so.

thumbnail.description: Clip thumbnail URL when provided by the archive.

continuationWindows.description: Windows to re-run this query against when maxRecords reaches its 3000 ceiling: the queried window split in two on a clock hour, with no shared second. Absent when no window is known or narrowing cannot reach further clips.

items.description: One window to re-query with the same query string.

endDatetime.description: End of this window in GDELT format YYYYMMDDHHMMSS.

startDatetime.description: Start of this window in GDELT format YYYYMMDDHHMMSS.

effectiveQuery.description: Echoed query string for use in follow-up calls.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `invalid_date_range`: Only one of startDatetime / endDatetime was supplied, one of them is not a real UTC calendar timestamp, or startDatetime is not earlier than endDatetime. `invalid_query`: GDELT rejected the query — no station was selected, or the query string is malformed. `gdelt_rate_limited`: GDELT rejected the request for its one-request-per-five-seconds limit, or too many requests were already queued for this one to start in time. `gdelt_unavailable`: GDELT TV API is unreachable or temporarily returned no usable data. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

limitClamp.description: Present only when the requested count exceeded the per-call cap: the call ran exactly as a call at the cap, and every count, notice, and continuation in this response reflects the applied value.

applied.description: The per-call cap the call ran with instead.

parameter.description: The count input that was clamped.

requested.description: The value the call asked for.

notice.description: Guidance on an incomplete or empty result. When no clips matched, the resolved timespan window and how to check station monitoring dates and choose an explicit window. When GDELT returned clips aired outside the requested window, how many were dropped. When the maxRecords cap was reached, raise maxRecords below the 3000 ceiling or narrow the date window at it. When a returned clip has no station ID, why: GDELT returned it without a station label, or its station catalog did not load or has no entry for the named label — with how to look the ID up. Absent when a non-empty result set is below the cap, no clip was dropped as out of window, and every clip carries its station ID.

staleResponse.description: Present only when the refetch of this exact request was refused, failed, or came back empty, and the response is GDELT's stored answer from fetchedAt instead. It holds nothing published after fetchedAt; a relative timespan covers the window ending at fetchedAt, not now. Absent on a live answer.

ageSeconds.description: Age of the stored answer when served, in whole seconds.

fetchedAt.description: ISO 8601 time GDELT returned the stored answer.

reason.description: Why the refetch was not used: GDELT rate-limited it, did not answer with data, or answered empty — which GDELT also does under load.

title: Get GDELT TV Clips
